issues.name: solana-moonpay-usdc-onramp
issues.description:
Let a card-only user (no USDC, no funded wallet) buy USDC on Solana via MoonPay and then start / keep funded an OpenRails recurring Solana subscription. MoonPay is a fiat->crypto on-ramp (iframe widget / @moonpay/moonpay-js / @moonpay/moonpay-react).

## Key findings (research 2026-06-03)
- USDC on Solana IS supported, currencyCode=`usdc_sol` (NOT bare `usdc`, which defaults to Ethereum), delivered to a user-supplied Solana address. Classic SPL mint = matches our engine.
- The user STILL needs a self-custody wallet (Phantom/Backpack): MoonPay only delivers tokens, it cannot SIGN the OpenRails SPL-delegation/subscribe tx. MoonPay's hosted wallet can't sign delegation -> require an external wallet.
- URL signing is REQUIRED whenever the widget URL carries walletAddress: HMAC-SHA256 over the query string keyed by the secret key (sk_), base64. So even minimal integration needs ONE backend route to sign URLs (frontend generateUrlForSigning -> backend HMAC -> updateSignature). pk_ is frontend, sk_ is backend-only.
- Webhooks (transaction_created/updated/failed, verify Moonpay-Signature-V2, de-dupe) are OPTIONAL for basic UX -- we can instead POLL the wallet's USDC ATA balance since the deliverable is an on-chain transfer to a known address.
- KYC always required; card fee ~up to 4.5% with a $3.99 minimum; min purchase ~$20-30; brutal on small amounts (a $10 buy can pay ~40% fee). Geo: 150+ countries, excludes LA/USVI + sanctioned; NY now OK (BitLicense).
- RECURRING-FUNDING GAP (central tension): MoonPay is a ONE-TIME buy; it does NOT auto-refill each period. Our engine pulls USDC every period via SPL delegation, so the ATA must STAY funded. Either pre-buy many periods up front (amortizes the fee/minimum) or re-onramp each period (bad). There is no MoonPay recurring on-ramp.
- STRATEGIC POSITION: a pure card user who wants recurring should usually just use OpenRails' existing Stripe/NMI card rails. Position MoonPay as a 'fund/top-up your Solana wallet' convenience for self-custody/crypto-native users + one-time top-ups to keep a Solana sub funded + hard-to-card regions + larger prepayments -- NOT as the recurring payment method. The recurring engine stays pure Solana; MoonPay is the bootstrap/top-up step.

Sources: dev.moonpay.com/docs (quickstart, signed-urls, web-sdk, buy params), npm @moonpay/moonpay-js + moonpay-react, support.moonpay.com simplified-buy-for-solana, moonpay.com/newsroom/usdc-solana-moonpay, docs.solanaappkit.com moonpay (usdc_sol), dev.moonpay.com webhooks + sandbox, moonpay.com/legal/pricing_disclosure.
tasks: [ ] Canonical flow: connect Phantom/Backpack -> read walletPubkey -> check USDC ATA balance -> if < (period amount x N)+buffer, show 'Buy USDC' -> launch MoonPay buy widget (currencyCode=usdc_sol, walletAddress=pubkey, signed URL) -> KYC+card -> USDC lands in ATA -> detect arrival -> user signs subscribe/delegation -> recurring pulls begin.

[ ] PHASE 1 (minimal): backend POST /moonpay/sign-url (holds sk_, HMAC-SHA256 the query string) + frontend 'Buy USDC on Solana' CTA gated on a low-ATA-balance check; detect funding by POLLING the ATA balance (no webhook infra); pre-fill baseCurrencyAmount = needed+buffer; sandbox first (environment=sandbox, pk_test_).

[ ] PHASE 2: embedded widget; lockAmount = subscriptionAmount x prefundPeriods + buffer (so the user funds N periods up front, amortizing fees); add webhook receiver (transaction_*, verify Moonpay-Signature-V2, de-dupe, correlate via externalTransactionId=sub/user id); low-balance 'top up' CTA on the subscription dashboard (MoonPay won't auto-refill).
[ ] Require an EXTERNAL signing wallet; explicitly disallow MoonPay's auto-created hosted wallet (can't sign delegation).

[ ] Surface pre-pull BALANCE HEALTH from the recurring engine so the UI can trigger a top-up before a pull would fail (engine likely already knows; just expose it). No change to delegation/pull logic; MoonPay is non-custodial and never holds OpenRails funds.
[ ] Geo-gate the CTA for unsupported locales (LA, USVI, sanctioned) using user-locale signals.

[ ] OPEN DECISIONS (user): (1) primary use = bootstrap-from-zero vs top-up existing sub? (2) prefund horizon (3/6/12 months)? (3) webhooks in phase 1 or defer? (4) where sk_ lives (OpenRails route vs edge fn)? (5) confirm external-wallet-required. (6) lock the USDC amount = needed+buffer? (7) honest framing: position as 'fund your wallet', keep steering pure-card users to Stripe/NMI.

issues.name: processor-routing-and-fallback-policy
issues.description:
Add deterministic processor selection and fallback policy so checkout can choose the best available rail for a tenant/product/tier/user context before creating a one-processor checkout session.

## Metadata

- Category: feature
- Status: planned
- Passes: false

## Motivation

- Hyperswitch wins on payment orchestration. OpenRails should not chase broad smart-routing, but customers do need basic processor redundancy and product/tenant-aware routing, especially high-risk merchants with Stripe plus NMI/Mobius/CCBill/Solana.
- Keep checkout sessions one-processor-at-a-time; route before session creation.

## Non-goals

- No ML routing.
- No 200-connector orchestration platform.
- No automatic retry to a second processor after a successful authorization attempt unless the processor contract makes that safe.

[ ] Decide precedence: explicit price/provider config > tenant policy > product/tier_group policy > global default.

## Motivation

- Lago is strongest at usage events, metrics, and invoices. OpenRails should not clone Lago, but customers using OpenRails for AI/API workloads need a clean event-to-credit-charge path instead of each host manually calculating all debits.
- This should reuse the current credit ledger, holds, capture/release, prepaid/arrears behavior, spend caps, and owner/actor model.

## Non-goals

- No invoice PDF/e-invoicing/tax product in this issue.
- No full Lago-style billing engine.
- No replacement for Tensorhub/gen-orchestrator pricing if those systems remain the pricing source of truth; support both host-computed and OpenRails-computed amounts.


--- DESIGN ADDENDUM (Lago/Hyperswitch competitive analysis, 2026-06-04) ---
Lago analysis confirms #289 is the right home for the NATIVE usage-pricing engine (do NOT delegate pricing to Stripe Meters — see #134). The cleanest, highest-value port is Lago's CHARGE-MODEL math, which are pure (units, properties)->amount functions with thorough spec files:
- standard (units x unit_amount), graduated (each tier at its own rate, summed), volume (one tier rate for the WHOLE qty), package (round up to package count x price), percentage (rate% + fixed_per_event, free-units, optional per-txn min/max), graduated_percentage, dynamic.
- Source to translate into Go table-tests: lago api/app/services/charge_models/{standard,graduated,volume,package,percentage,graduated_percentage,dynamic}_service.rb + api/spec/services/charge_models/*_spec.rb + amount_details/range_graduated_service.rb + factory.rb.
- PRECISION: Lago carries amount_cents (rounded) AND precise_amount_cents (un-rounded BigDecimal); rounds ONCE at the fee edge. OpenRails is integer-cents end-to-end -> adopt shopspring/decimal (or big.Rat) INSIDE the pricing package and round only when writing the debit/fee, else tiered/percentage pricing compounds rounding error across many small events.
- Store the model + tier bands as JSONB 'properties' on the pricing rule (per credit_type/product/price). Keep the existing host-priced vs OpenRails-priced two-mode contract.
Effort: ~1 Go pkg internal/modules/usage/pricing with a ChargeModel interface + ~6 impls, ported from the specs. BUILD THIS FIRST for usage billing.

issues.name: provider-certification-matrix
issues.description:
Publish and maintain a provider certification matrix for Stripe, NMI/Mobius, CCBill, and Solana that records exactly which customer-visible flows are supported, sandbox/devnet tested, live/test-mode tested, and known-limited.

## Metadata

- Category: product
- Status: planned
- Passes: false

## Motivation

- OpenRails' strongest differentiator is deep support for real non-Stripe rails, especially NMI-compatible high-risk gateways like Mobius. Customers need confidence that the specific flows they care about actually work.
- This should become both documentation and an executable certification harness where practical.
tasks: MATRIX DESIGN:

[ ] Define provider capabilities and certification statuses: not_supported, manual_only, unit_tested, integration_tested, sandbox_certified, live_test_mode_certified, devnet_certified, production_certified.

[ ] Define flows to track: catalog/product push, price/recurring-plan push, one-time checkout, recurring checkout, vault/tokenization, rebill, cancellation, deferred cancellation, refund, dispute/chargeback, webhook handling, subscription sync/backfill, catalog drift detection.

[ ] Include processor-specific notes: NMI product/prices are local while recurring prices push as NMI recurring plans; CCBill catalog actions may be manual; Solana recurring requires on-chain readback/devnet certification.
DOCS:
[ ] Add docs/providers.md or equivalent with the current matrix and exact tested commands.

[ ] Add NMI-compatible gateway guidance: required security_key, Collect.js/tokenization key if needed, direct/query endpoints, test_mode behavior, and how Mobius/NMI white-label accounts map to the same interface.
[ ] Add troubleshooting for common provider failures: bad endpoint, key belongs to different gateway user, sandbox URL not supported, recurring plan query mismatch, webhook signature failure.
EXECUTABLE CERTIFICATION:
[ ] Add or formalize focused integration tests for NMI/Mobius sale, vault, recurring plan create/readback, and query API.
[ ] Add Stripe test-mode catalog apply + subscription sync certification steps.
[ ] Add Solana devnet read-back certification for plan accounts and recurring lifecycle.
[ ] Add CCBill manual-action verification path so unsupported remote catalog operations surface as pending_manual_actions rather than errors.
PROCESS:
[ ] Make certification matrix updates part of provider-related PRs.
[ ] Record last verified date, environment, and command for each provider flow without exposing secrets.

issues.name: processor-capability-metadata

## Metadata

- Category: architecture
- Status: planned

## Motivation
